# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Emerson Foster**
[Street address]
[City], South Carolina [ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-16**
- **Member:** Emerson Foster
- **Member ID:** W201693421
- **Reference number:** POC-9A43271177-74690
- **Service denied:** Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
- **Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my total knee replacement (CPT 27447), which Cigna denied on 2026-08-16 under reference number POC-9A43271177-74690. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file do address the plan's own criteria in Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this surgery is needed.

Below I set out the plan's published criteria and the matching evidence from my records. Where a record is already in the file, I have said so; I am also re-sending the documents listed at the end of this letter so that nothing is missing from the review.

## The plan's imaging criteria

The policy states:

> "Imaging or arthroscopic findings show EITHER of the following:"

and, as one of those options:

> "severe unicompartmental (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral), bicompartmental, or tricompartmental osteoarthritis as evidenced by ANY of the following:"

with the first listed finding being:

> "Kellgren-Lawrence Grade III or IV radiographic findings"

**What my records show:** Weight-bearing knee radiographs taken 2026-07-21 show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing, read as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4. That is a Grade IV radiographic finding, in more than one compartment, on the exact imaging study type the policy asks about.

The policy's other listed findings are not the basis of my request, and I am not claiming them: my file does not describe a fracture of the distal femur, arthroscopic findings, MRI findings, or avascular necrosis. I rely on the Kellgren-Lawrence criterion above, which the policy states on its own terms is sufficient when the findings show severe osteoarthritis.

## The plan's symptom criteria

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

> "loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

**What my records show:** I have had 18 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest — far longer than the three months the policy describes. My records document that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and that I wake 3–4 times a night because of the pain. On examination my knee shows varus alignment, crepitus and effusion, with range of motion limited to 5 to 100 degrees. These are documented losses of knee function that interfere with ordinary daily activities.

If the reviewer needs my walking distance stated in the specific terms the policy uses, I am glad to have that recorded and submitted: [distance I can walk before pain stops me, to be documented by my treating provider].

## The plan's conservative-care criterion

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

**What my records show:** I completed supervised physical therapy directed at quadriceps strengthening and range of motion — 20 visits over 16 weeks, from 2026-03-29 to 2026-07-19 — documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is longer than the three months the policy requires. I also took NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-24 that gave me only about four weeks of partial relief. My pain has continued to progress despite all of it.

Because this provider-directed non-surgical management was completed and did not work, the policy's exception language — "Criteria exception: Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate. The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate." — does not need to be reached in my case.

## Preoperative optimization

The policy includes this note:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

My records document that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## A request about what was found to be missing

The denial says the documentation was incomplete, but it does not tell me which specific criterion Cigna found unsupported or which document it was looking for. I would also note that several of the criteria I have quoted above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions in the full policy that were not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. So that I can respond precisely rather than guessing, I ask Cigna to identify in writing the specific criteria in Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 that it applied and the specific records it found missing. If a single document is the gap, I will obtain it promptly.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Cigna overturn the denial dated 2026-08-16 and authorize total knee replacement, CPT 27447, as requested by Dr. Marchetti. In the alternative, I ask that the request be returned for a full clinical review against the criteria quoted above, with my imaging report, physical therapy discharge note, and office notes in front of the reviewer.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-12, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, and/or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; the phone number for questions is 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member card.

**Documents enclosed:**
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report dated 2026-07-21
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-03-29 to 2026-07-19 (20 visits)
- Office/operative planning notes from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records, including the corticosteroid injection of 2026-04-24
- [Any additional records my provider's office sends under separate cover]

Thank you for reviewing this again. Please send your decision in writing to the address above.

Sincerely,

_________________________
**Emerson Foster**
Member ID: W201693421
Date of birth: [DOB]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
